_comment: Frontend-state payloads captured from a REAL local-operator backend, so the
cost and context mirrors in src/renderer/src/features/chat/session-status/
are pinned against what the owner actually sends rather than against what a
reader of the Python thought it sends.
How this was captured (repeatable):
1. An ISOLATED backend, never the operator's live one:
LOCAL_OPERATOR_CONFIG_DIR=<tmp>/config LOCAL_OPERATOR_HOME=<tmp>/home \
LOCAL_OPERATOR_DESKTOP_TOKEN=<token> local-operator serve --port 1179
with a minimal config.yml naming a provider, and one credential line
copied into <tmp>/config/credentials.env.
2. POST /v1/desktop/sessions to create a session in that tmp cwd.
3. An SSE reader on GET /v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/events held open while a
prompt was POSTed to .../messages and /model and /effort were POSTed to
.../commands. The accounting fields arrive ONLY as `frontend.update`
changes on that stream -- the cold `GET /v1/desktop/sessions/{id}`
snapshot reports them all null, which is why a fixture taken from the
snapshot alone would have pinned nothing.
4. Each capture below is the merged snapshot+updates state at that moment.
Backend version at capture: 0.54.14. Model: openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini,
then openrouter/openai/gpt-5.
The `expect` blocks are what the TUI would render for the same state, per
the symbols named in session-cost.ts and session-context.ts.
Round 3: every `modelName` was RECOMPUTED through the real
format_model_label. The round-1 values were the desktop's own output at the
time, which is why they agreed with a chip that disagreed with the band -
an expectation copied from the code under test rather than from its source.
